entry.title: Sub-Quadratic Sparse Attention via Block-Spectral Routing at 1M Context. Exact self-attention scales as $O(L^2)$ in sequence length $L$, bottlenecking million-token inference.
entry.summary:
Exact self-attention scales as $O(L^2)$ in sequence length $L$, bottlenecking million-token inference. We propose Block-Spectral Routing (BSR), which projects key-value blocks onto a low-rank Chebyshev basis and routes queries to the top-$k$ spectral buckets in $O(L \log L)$ time, matching full FlashAttention-3 accuracy on needle-in-a-haystack and code reasoning benchmarks with $4.7\times$ lower KV-cache bandwidth.

Source: Hugging Face Daily Papers · Tags: #llm #inference #ml-theory

entry.title: Verified Tool-Use Trajectories for Multi-Step Coding Agents via Formal Preconditions
entry.summary:
Autonomous coding agents frequently execute destructive shell or filesystem mutations when intermediate hypotheses fail. We attach lightweight Hoare-style state preconditions to MCP tool schemas, pruning invalid action branches before execution and raising SWE-bench Verified pass rates by $11.4\%$ with $32\%$ fewer token rollouts.

Source: arXiv AI (cs.LG) · Tags: #agents #llm #formal-proofs

entry.title: Sharp Non-Asymptotic Generalization Bounds for LoRA Fine-Tuning Under Heavy-Tailed Gradients
entry.summary:
Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) empirically resists overfitting even when fine-tuned on small domain corpora with high gradient variance. We derive non-asymptotic PAC-Bayes generalization bounds scaling with the stable rank $\text{sr}(BA) \ll r$, explaining why rank-$16$ adapters match full fine-tuning sample complexity.

Source: JMLR / stat.ML · Tags: #ml-theory #llm #probability-stats
